I think fat free Greek Yogurt fails as a dip on almost every level. It's sharp and sour like yogurt, but it's not creamy, and you're constantly reminded that you're eating yogurt. It's awful. So I started experimenting with Morinaga Silken Tofu because it was on deep discount at Costco. I made one recipe that got upvoted on Reddit:

Country Fresh French Onion Chip Dip Copy

  • 1.5 tbsp dry minced onion
  • 1 small onion, microwaved 2 minutes on high
  • 1 tbsp Brazilian fried garlic (alho frito)
  • 2 tbsp vinegar
  • 1 tbsp pickle juice from kosher dills
  • 1/2 tsp dill
  • 1 cube silken tofu
  • Salt
  • Black pepper

Blend until smooth.

I got bored with that though, and I wanted something easy, and this was on sale at Meijer: Hidden Valley Greek Yogurt Ranch Dip. It's the easiest thing in the world, put the dip mix in the blender, put a block of tofu on top, and blend for like a minute. Put it in the refrigerator for an hour or overnight for best results.

This is good stuff.

I made this last night and was pretty good and allows for tweaking. I'll try it again slightly modified next time as the onion was too strong for me and overpowered certain bites. I really want to try the HV greek yogurt ranch dip now.

Do animals have languages? Would animals of the same (or similar) species from different parts of the world be able to communicate?

I love reading research about this sort of thing; generally anything about how smart animals are. I remember some research showed that the clicks and sounds whales and dolphins made weren't random, that they referenced specific things. It went on to show that the same species of whale used the same clicks/sounds with very minor variations. Basically dialects and accents. check this out http://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2011/05/110512104252.htm

or just google "whale accent" or " whale dialect" some really interesting stuff

Interesting. I don't know much about whales and the range in which each one swims, but I would've thought that aquatic animals would be able to travel further than land animals, so they'd be more likely to be able to communicate even if they are from different areas. Do you know anything about land animals' communications?

Here is a link to an article that discusses bird communication: Crows show off social skills

I feel that land and sea animals do communication. Their languages may not be as sophisticated as our own but are a form of passing information.

This may be of interest : "Some vinkeniers claim that finches from the different regions of Belgium sing in different dialects; with birds from the Dutch-speaking Flanders singing "in Dutch" and those from the French-speaking Wallonia singing undesirably "in French"."
